mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the federal funds rate increased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over the last two quarters indicates strong economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where real GDP increased for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreased by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production index by more than 2% over the last two months signals a weakening supply chain, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to be negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the industrial production index decreased by more than 2% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 10% over the last two months signals strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where housing starts increased by more than 10% over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment increases by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% within the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP and a simultaneous increase in retail and food services sales by more than 1% over the last quarter signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.
